subject: Kestrel pilot: charter, evaluation approach, and ownership
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@kestrelhealth.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@kestrelhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Kestrel pilot: charter, evaluation approach, and ownership

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a concrete pilot approach so we can lock timelines and responsibilities. I tried to balance Kestrel’s regulatory constraints with a pragmatic path to measurable results.

High level recap
- Goal: Reduce triage response errors in the clinical intake assistant by 40% vs current rule-based baseline while keeping P95 latency under 500ms and hallucination rate below 2%.
- Scope: 10k historical intake records (de-identified) + 3 live clinical agents in the shadow window.

Recommended evaluation approach (two-phase hybrid)
1) Offline evaluation (week 0–1):
   - Ben will ingest 5k labeled records from Kestrel (we’ll provide the ingestion script).
   - Metrics: per-intent precision/recall, top-1 classification F1, false-positives that indicate hallucination, and token-level latency estimates on a simulated 8k-token day.
   - Pass gate: weighted score >= 0.72 (weights: F1 50%, hallucination penalty 30%, latency penalty 20%).
2) Online shadow (week 2):
   - 10% live traffic mirrored to Redwood inference in a no-impact mode. Marcus will wire metric collection (latency, error signals, operator flags).
   - Acceptance: no production-impact incidents, average live P95 latency <= 450ms, operator-reported false-positive rate <= 2.5%.

Ownership (who does what)
- Ava (me): project lead / exec updates / final acceptance decision.
- Ben: data intake + offline eval orchestration + report.
- Marcus: infra, access, shadow routing, and monitoring dashboard.

Attachments: Kestrel_POC_Charter_v1.pdf (charter), Kestrel_Success_Criteria.xlsx (metrics & thresholds).

Next steps / asks (please reply with confirmations where applicable)
- Elena: confirm procurement contact for a one-off data transfer NDA and whether IT needs a specific SFTP profile.
- Kestrel: provide the first 5k de-identified records by 2027-07-19.
- Ben: will send ingestion template by EOD tomorrow.

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Thu 7/15 to cover data format, access, and checkpoints.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Elena / Tom —

Great questions. Short answers and an updated rubric baked into the plan below. I attached a CSV-style rubric (kestrel_eval_rubric_v1.csv) and updated the Success_Criteria workbook.

1) Grading rubric (example and pass gates)
   - Offline weighted score = 0.5 * F1 + 0.3 * (1 - hallucination_rate) + 0.2 * latency_score
   - latency_score = max(0, 1 - (P95_latency_ms - 200)/800) clipped to [0,1] (so lower latency improves the score).
   - Example threshold: F1 = 0.78, hallucination_rate = 0.015 -> weighted score = 0.5*0.78 + 0.3*(0.985) + 0.2*(0.7) = 0.715 + 0.2955 + 0.14 = 1.1505 (normalized to 0–1 in the CSV; pass >= 0.72).

2) Shadow safety & PHI masking
   - We can run shadow with field-level masking. Marcus: Redwood supports field redaction inline during the ingest/streaming step; we will not persist masked fields in our cluster and will write only hashed IDs to logs. Retention and encryption: yes, we support cross-account KMS; logs can be stored in Kestrel’s bucket with 90-day retention. I will circulate a short Ops checklist for SFTP/KMS access.

3) Timeline adjustment
   - 7/22 dataset delivery is OK. Updated milestones:
     - 2027-07-22: Kestrel delivers 5k de-identified records and schema.
     - 2027-07-25: Redwood completes offline run and shares report.
     - 2027-08-02 - 2027-08-09: Shadow window (7 days), 10% mirrored traffic, ops monitoring.

4) Ownership (finalized)
   - Ava Chen: project lead, final acceptance, executive updates.
   - Ben Carter: data pipeline, offline run, report (ben.carter@redwood.com).
   - Marcus Lin: shadow routing, KMS/S3 ops, retention policy (marcus.lin@redwood.com).

Action items (short)
- Elena: confirm procurement contact and SFTP/KMS constraints (reply by 7/16).
- Kestrel: deliver dataset + schema by 7/22 to the secure intake endpoint (Ben will send instructions).
- Redwood: provide offline results by 7/25 and schedule a 30-min review on 7/27 or 7/28.

Attachments: kestrel_eval_rubric_v1.csv (scoring, normalization, example calc).

If this aligns I’ll put the kickoff on calendars for 7/23 9am PT (30m) to walk the ingestion checklist and approval path.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
